solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Use a drill

definitions.meaning: to use a right or a muscle is to put it into action, to exert it
a drill is a set of practice movements, as soldiers do on the parade ground

explanation.surface: An instruction to pick up a power drill and get on with the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: exerting a power is putting it to use, and a drill is a routine of training movements.

clue.text: Catch the blame after net is damaged

indicators.note: after puts the word for blame behind the rearranged net
a net that is damaged has its letters knocked into a new order

parts.note: the word net, taken as written, is the fodder
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: A fisherman gets blamed once his net is torn and the catch escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is damaged' signals the anagram, and 'after' places the word for blame at the end; 'the rap' is the idiom for blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch someone out by a trick is to snare them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Cosmetic watchdog?

parts.note: to eye is to watch closely, the first half of the word
to shadow is to dog someone, following them, the second half of the word

explanation.surface: A cosmetic product named as if it were a consumer watchdog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watchdog' looks like one noun, but its two halves are read separately as verbs meaning to observe and to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured powder or cream brushed onto the lids is a make-up product, a cosmetic.

clue.text: Saucy thing to cut

parts.note: a pickled flower bud found in tartare sauce, and also a playful leap

explanation.surface: Something cheeky that one is allowed to cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' suggests cheekiness but points to sauce; 'cut a caper' is an idiom for frisking about.
explanation.definitionFit: The pickled bud goes into sauces, and the idiom 'cut a caper' means to skip or frolic.

clue.text: A parliamentary term?

parts.note: looks like a request for a piece of Westminster jargon, but means a period during which parliament sits

explanation.surface: A query about the vocabulary used in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' reads as a word or expression; here it is a stretch of time when the house meets.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament's sitting year is divided into sittings, each a period of business.

clue.text: Neglect Dad's drink

parts.note: Pa is a familiar word for Dad, with the possessive 's
to sup is to drink, especially in sips

explanation.surface: Someone ignores the drink their father has poured.
explanation.definitionFit: To let an opportunity go by unused is to neglect it; the phrasal verb is a near synonym.

clue.text: Fussy aunt boils her washing, perhaps

indicators.note: a fussy aunt fidgets, so her letters together with those of boils are set in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A particular aunt boils her laundry to get it clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fussy' mixes AUNT and BOILS; 'her' is only a link; 'perhaps' marks washing as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means acts of bodily cleansing, and washing oneself is a typical instance.

clue.text: It supports parade with conscious pride

definitions.meaning: a rod or brace in a framework that bears weight
to walk in a swaggering, showy way

explanation.surface: Something that props up a show of self-satisfied marching.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace in a structure bears load, and to swagger is to walk with showy self-importance.

clue.text: Friend with odd ideas for defence

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: odd ideas are strange ones, so the letters of ideas are put out of order

explanation.surface: A friend offers eccentric suggestions to help with a defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' is the anagram signal, not a description of the friend; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence of pointed stakes was built as protection around a settlement or fort.

clue.text: Spring a lock outside and make an entry

indicators.note: the word for a lock goes outside the word for a spring

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A burglar springs a lock from outside to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring a lock' suggests picking it, but spring is a mineral water source and the lock is of hair; 'outside' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To go onto land without permission is to enter where one should not, an unlawful entry.

clue.text: Free for-all sort of arrangement

indicators.note: letters that are set free are loosened into a different order

explanation.surface: A chaotic free-for-all described as a kind of arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges the letters of FOR-ALL; the free-for-all of the surface is broken apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement of flowers in a vase is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Street food?

definitions.meaning: ... Street was a London street of hack writers, a former name of Milton Street

explanation.surface: A question about food bought from street stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: Grub Street was a London street of struggling hack writers, so the word is both part of a street name and slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for food that is also the first part of the name of a famous London street.

clue.text: Shrink from hunting initially with wild boar around

indicators.note: the rearranged boar goes around the first letter of hunting
a wild boar runs loose, so its letters are scattered
initially means take the opening letter of hunting

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from hunting, at first, with a wild boar circling them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns BOAR into ABOR, and 'around' sets it about H.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink from something in disgust is to loathe it, a synonym.

clue.text: Annoys girl with awkward tries to embrace

indicators.note: the jumbled tries wraps its arms around the girl's name
awkward tries are clumsy ones, so the letters of tries are jumbled

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is annoyed by someone's clumsy attempts to hug her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' is the anagram signal and 'to embrace' the container signal; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy someone is to get on their nerves, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fresh air — and that's essential for this man

indicators.note: a fresh version is a new one, so the letters of air and and are made anew

explanation.surface: Someone who insists that fresh air is vital to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' rearranges AIR and AND; 'that's essential for' is link padding pointing to the man.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a man's first name, so it can stand for a man indicated by the clue.

clue.text: Foundry club doesn't go on strike

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
someone who doesn't strike keeps working, so works

explanation.surface: A foundry's union decides not to walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundry is a factory where metal is cast, a place for smelting and forging metal.

clue.text: Literary prop

parts.note: seems to mean a stage device in a novel, but is a physical support that keeps books upright on a shelf

explanation.surface: A device or crutch used in writing fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prop' suggests a plot device; it is a literal support for books.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy block placed at the end of a row of books holds them upright.

clue.text: This military order looks fine

parts.note: eyes means looks at, as a verb
right means fine or all right

explanation.surface: A parade-ground command that appears perfectly acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill command telling a marching unit to turn their heads to salute.

clue.text: Came to blows — no longer retained

definitions.meaning: had a fight, scrap being slang for a fight

explanation.surface: Fighting broke out, and someone was dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a fist fight, so fought; and plans discarded as useless have been thrown out.

clue.text: Unscrupulous operators involved in Western films

definitions.meaning: dodgy tradesmen who do shoddy work, in British slang
the cattle-herding heroes of Hollywood Westerns

explanation.surface: Crooks working in the making of Westerns.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage the word also means rogue builders or tradesmen who overcharge for poor work.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogue tradesmen are called this in Britain, and the mounted cattle herders feature in every Western.

clue.text: It may run out in time

definitions.text: It may run out in time

parts.words: It may run out in time
parts.note: sounds like a supply that will be exhausted eventually, but describes the grains trickling through an hourglass that measures time

explanation.surface: Something that will be used up sooner or later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out' suggests being used up; in an hourglass the grains literally run out as time is measured.
explanation.definitionFit: An hourglass or egg timer is filled with fine grains that flow through to mark time.

clue.text: Method of betting trying to avoid betting slips?

definitions.text: Method of betting trying to avoid betting slips?

parts.words: Method of betting trying to avoid betting slips?
parts.note: a gambler's scheme meant to stop losing, with slips read as mistakes rather than the paper tickets

explanation.surface: A scheme for wagering that sidesteps bookmakers' paper slips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slips' looks like the paper tickets from a bookmaker but means errors in betting.
explanation.definitionFit: A punter's planned method of staking bets, meant to beat the odds, is given this name.

clue.text: Composer lifts manuscript with a neat amendment

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word lays it upwards, so it reads backwards
an amendment alters, so the letters of a and neat are revised

explanation.surface: A composer picks up his score and tidies it up neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifts' turns MS into SM; 'amendment' rearranges A NEAT into ETANA. Bedřich Smetana was a Czech composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was the nineteenth-century Czech composer of Má vlast.

clue.text: More unfortunate choice in the marriage ceremony

definitions.meaning: the vow 'for richer, for ...' offers a pair of alternatives

explanation.surface: An unlucky decision made at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Less well off means more pitiable, and the wedding vow pairs richer with this word.

clue.text: A cut limits inadequate grant

indicators.note: the word for cut limits, encloses, the word for inadequate

parts.note: to lance is to cut, as a surgeon lances a boil
low means inadequate, as in low supplies

explanation.surface: A reduction caps a grant that was already too small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a noun for a reduction, but here it is the verb to pierce, as with a surgeon's blade; 'limits' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum of money granted regularly for expenses is a grant, a synonym.

clue.text: Sort of dancer at university to enjoy drink?

parts.note: a lap dancer is one kind of dancer
up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: A dancer studying at university who likes a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' for being at university is British usage, as in 'up at Oxford'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapping a drink like a cat, or accepting something eagerly, is to enjoy it with relish.

clue.text: Silent comedy film-star

parts.note: seems to mean a star of silent-era comedies, but names the Marx brother who never spoke on screen

explanation.surface: A star of the silent comedy era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silent' suggests the silent-film era; this star appeared in talkies but never spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marx brother with the curly wig and horn who played a mute character on screen.

clue.text: A hit I made in Caribbean republic

indicators.note: the letters of a hit I are made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a smash hit they had in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges A HIT I; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The country occupying the western third of Hispaniola is a republic in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Press for identity documents?

definitions.meaning: official ... proving who one is, the question mark marking an example

explanation.surface: A demand to see someone's identity documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers are the press, and identification documents are a person's credentials or ID.

clue.text: Stay well away from work

parts.note: sounds like advice to keep clear of the office, but means to stay off while well, feigning illness

explanation.surface: Advice to keep far away from the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' reads as an intensifier but means healthy: staying off work while in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirkers who pretend to be ill to avoid duty are said to do this.

clue.text: Put down for PE, does work-out

indicators.note: letters given a work-out are exercised and shaken into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone signed up for gym class performs an exercise routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work-out' rearranges PE and DOES; PE is physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down a ruler is to overthrow them, to remove from office.

clue.text: Container crates in bad state

indicators.note: crates in a bad state are broken up, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A container arrives in crates that are damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad state' rearranges CRATES IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a metal can or tin for storing tea or other goods, a type of container.
